forecast-period.text: A trough will move across SA today ahead of a high pressure ridge that will build in the wake. A cold front will then slip across southern coasts late Monday and early Tuesday, before the high moves across waters to the south to be centred over Victoria by Thursday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms extending across the west and south, clearing from the west throughout the day. Thunderstorms possibly gusty about the eastern districts and possible about the far northwest later. Maximum temperatures above average, tending near average in the southwest. North to northwesterly winds ahead of the change, freshening at times and shifting southwest to southeasterly from the west throughout the day.

Possible morning fog about the Agricultural Areas and West Coast. Showers and thunderstorms in the far west. Isolated showers developing about southern coastal districts during the afternoon and extending over the remainder of the Southern Agricultural Area from the evening. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, tending near average elsewhere. Southwest to southeasterly winds, freshening about the coast later.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far northwest, with isolated light showers possible about the Southern Agricultural Area clearing by the afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the coast and central and northern inland parts.

text.p: Dry and mostly sunny. Maximum temperatures below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: less than 2 mm about the Northern Agricultural Area, reaching up to 2 to 5 mm about the Southern Agricultural Area and 5 to 10 mm about southern coasts, ranges and the South East. Local heavier falls are possible between 5 to 15 mm. 5 to 15 mm possible about parts of the west, with local heavier falls between 20 to 40 mm possible in the far west.
